lines.text: In eighteen sixty-nine, workers digging a well in New York
found a giant stone man, almost ten feet tall.
But he was no ancient giant.
A cigar maker named George Hull
argued with a preacher about giants in the Bible.
So Hull decided to make one.
He had a huge block of stone cut in Iowa,
and a sculptor carved it into a giant.
Then he buried it on a farm in Cardiff,
When diggers finally hit the stone foot,
People paid twenty-five cents to see him.
Even the showman P. T. Barnum
Then Hull confessed, and it was all a hoax.
Today the giant is still on display in Cooperstown.
